Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months elapsed since the prior cervical decompression or fusion at an adjacent level

Symptoms must include BOTH: (a) clinically significant daily pain causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND (b) unremitting radicular pain to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical examination must demonstrate ANY of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor weakness of biceps or triceps, reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve‑root tension sign (e.g., positive Spurling’s maneuver), OR unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs for ≥6 weeks; provider‑directed exercise program (PT, chiropractic, MD‑prescribed) for ≥6 weeks; epidural steroid injection or selective nerve‑root block at the same level(s) as the proposed surgery

Imaging requirements: (a) plain cervical spine flexion/extension lateral X‑rays demonstrating successful decompression and fusion at the prior operative level; (b) MRI or CT of the cervical spine showing neural structure compression at the proposed adjacent level that is concordant with symptoms and caused by herniated disc material, synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)

Documentation of nicotine‑free status: either never‑smoker or abstinent from all tobacco/nicotine products for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery, verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range

Symptoms must include ANY of: upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting, hand clumsiness); gait disturbance; new‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; frequent falls

Physical examination must demonstrate ANY of: abnormal grip‑and‑release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand appearance
MRI or CT must show findings concordant with the individual's symptoms and exam and be caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as defined for radiculopathy (never‑smoker or ≥6‑week abstinence with objective cotinine verification)

Non-Indications: Less than six (6) months since the prior cervical decompression or fusion at the adjacent level
Absence of the required symptom severity (no daily functional impairment or no unremitting radicular pain for radiculopathy; no myelopathic symptoms for myelopathy)
Lack of any objective physical‑exam findings that correlate with the reported symptoms
Failure to complete the mandated trial of conservative therapy (≥6 weeks of at least two modalities) when not contraindicated
Imaging that does not demonstrate neural compression at the proposed level or shows incomplete fusion at the prior level
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Active tobacco use without documented cessation and objective cotinine test within normal limits
Inadequate or missing flexion/extension cervical X‑rays proving successful prior fusion
Important criteria & exceptions: Objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) must be performed within six (6) weeks prior to the planned surgery and reported as within the normal range for the assay used
If a patient cannot tolerate a specific conservative modality (e.g., medication adverse effects), the requirement of two modalities may be satisfied with the remaining eligible therapies
Both radiculopathy and myelopathy indications require documented successful fusion at the prior operative level; failure of that fusion excludes the adjacent‑segment procedure
Multi‑level ACDF is permissible only if each level independently meets all indication criteria
Behavioral health clearance must be documented by a qualified mental‑health professional stating that no unmanaged disorder exists
Documentation required: Operative report from the prior cervical decompression or fusion, specifying the level(s) operated on and confirmation of successful fusion
Plain cervical spine flexion and extension lateral X‑ray images (and radiology report) demonstrating successful fusion at the prior level
Current cervical spine MRI or CT report of the adjacent level(s) showing neural compression (herniated disc, cyst, stenosis, osteophytes) and correlating with symptoms
Comprehensive physical examination note documenting sensory deficits, motor weakness, reflex changes, or positive nerve‑root tension signs, as well as functional impairment due to pain
Pain and functional assessment documenting daily clinically significant pain and impact on activities of daily living
Medication administration record or prescription history confirming use of at least two of the following for ≥6 weeks: prescription analgesics/steroids, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs
Physical therapy, chiropractic, or other provider‑directed exercise program note confirming ≥6 weeks of supervised therapy
Epidural steroid injection or selective nerve‑root block procedure report(s) performed at the same level(s) as the proposed surgery (if utilized)
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming absence of unmanaged major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid use disorder, or alcohol use disorder
Smoking cessation documentation and objective cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) performed ≤6 weeks before surgery, showing values within the normal reference range
Current MRI/CT radiology report of the proposed surgical level(s) confirming compression consistent with the clinical picture
